page_title: Command Book - Manage Long-Running Terminal Commands

sources.entry: Command Book - A terminal companion for long-running terminal commands (freemium)

summary.name: Command Book
summary.one_liner: A native macOS app and CLI that tracks long-running terminal commands (dev servers, databases, workers) started by you or AI agents, so you can check their status, read their output, and stop them reliably.
use_cases: Keep dev servers, databases and workers running without juggling Terminal tabs
Let an AI agent start, check and stop a local server without leaving orphaned processes
Save frequently used commands with their directory and environment variables
Read back output from a previous background run
summary.what_it_does: Command Book keeps a registry of processes started through it, from either its GUI or its CLI, so status checks and stop requests refer to real tracked handles. Commands can be saved with name, working directory, environment variables and pre-commands, and launched by click or by slug. The CLI offers run, start (background), wait (block until a URL or port responds), logs, status (with JSON output), stop, list, new, edit and open. Output is captured to disk so logs survive app quits and restarts, and processes can be relaunched after a restart. Auto-restart can bring back crashed processes, and a keyboard command palette (⌘K) and ⌘F search are included.
notable: Single registry shared by the GUI, the CLI and AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor), with a Claude Code skill installable from Settings
Native Swift and SwiftUI app, notarized and signed, about 21 MB on disk and 73 MB in memory, with no Electron
One-time purchase option with no subscription and no account required, per the page
caveats: Free edition is limited to 5 saved commands, 10 ad-hoc commands and 25,000 lines of output; unlimited commands, group commands and 500,000 lines require the one-time purchase
Only sees processes that Command Book launched; status and stop will not find processes started some other way
